Wednesday, November 25

Game recap

VGK5EDM3Final: VGK 5, EDM 3

The Oilers came home to stop the bleeding and needed all of six minutes to reopen it. Jack Eichel scored on the power play at 6:13, Trevor Connelly made it 2-0 unassisted three minutes later, and Edmonton spent the second period climbing back: Colton Dach at 3:03, then Connor McDavid's 14th with 19 seconds left to tie it. The reward for all that work was Nic Dowd, who picked 2:08 of the third for his first goal of the season. Eichel got his second at 5:29, Vasily Podkolzin answered 16 seconds later with his 14th, and Connelly's empty-netter gave him two goals and an assist. Carter Hart made 21 saves on 24 shots, Devon Levi 22 on 26. Vegas is 15-6-5 and three points back of first with a game in hand. Edmonton has dropped four straight after a 17-3-3 start. The Oilers usually wait until June to let everybody down; this year they're getting it done before Thanksgiving.

Tuesday, November 24

Game recap

CBJ2NJD3Final: CBJ 2, NJD 3

Two days after getting the hook in St. Louis, Connor Hellebuyck got the easy shift: 19 saves on 21 shots as the Devils held off Columbus 3-2. New Jersey did its damage early. Timo Meier opened it at 4:59 off the new top line with Jack Hughes and Connor Brown, his goal in a fourth straight game, and Brenden Dillon scored his first of the year three minutes later. Charlie Coyle cut it to 2-1 before the first was out, Brown made it 3-1 in the second, and Mikael Pyyhtia scored shorthanded with 14 seconds left in the period to make it interesting. Then nobody scored for 20 minutes. Zach Werenski logged 30:53 and put six shots on net, Cam Talbot stopped 27 of 30, and the Devils are 16-8-0. Columbus is 9-13-0 and gets the rematch Wednesday at home, where 2.55 goals a game, second-fewest in the league, will have to stretch a little further.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

LAK2MTL1Final: LAK 2, MTL 1

The Kings walked into the Bell Centre at 7-12-2 and walked out with a 2-1 win, which is about the rudest thing a team that low in the Pacific can do to a crowd in Montreal. Darcy Kuemper did most of the work: 29 saves on 30 shots. Alex Laferriere scored on the power play in the first off Quinton Byfield and Artemi Panarin, Alex Newhook tied it in the second, and Trevor Moore scored the winner at 14:57 of the second from Erik Haula and Joel Armia. Then the Canadiens spent a scoreless third finding out Kuemper wasn't moving. Jakub Dobes stopped 20 of 22 for the Canadiens, who have lost two straight and are 5-4-1 in their last 10. Los Angeles is 8-12-2. Montreal is still third in the Atlantic, but losing at home to the Kings is the kind of thing the Bell Centre remembers longer than the standings do.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

CGY1OTT2Final: CGY 1, OTT 2

Calgary outshot Ottawa 36-31 and lost anyway, because Linus Ullmark stopped 35 of them. The Senators got both of their goals in the last eight minutes of the first: Michael Amadio scored unassisted at 12:16, and Shane Pinto made it 2-0 at 17:37 for his 10th. Pinto had a full night. He also dropped the gloves with Joel Hanley at 12:17 of the third, then got to watch Matt Coronato score on the power play at 15:40 to make Ullmark's night a little less peaceful. That was all the Flames had. Devin Cooley stopped 29 of 31 in a game he deserved better from. Ottawa is 16-6-3, first in the Atlantic and 7-1-2 in its last 10. Calgary is 10-13-2 and has scored 2.44 goals a game, which is how you outshoot a team and go home with one goal and a fight to show for it.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

TOR4NYI2Final: TOR 4, NYI 2

The Maple Leafs won a hockey game. Write down the date. Down 2-0 on Long Island after Anthony Duclair scored in the first and Mathew Barzal got his first goal of the season in the second, Toronto scored four straight for its first win in 10 games. Dakota Joshua got one back in the second, Chris Tanev tied it 3:52 into the third with his first of the year, and Gavin McKenna scored the winner at 8:55 with an extra skater on, his seventh. Easton Cowan put it in the empty net. Auston Matthews' assist on Tanev's goal ran his road point streak to 10 games to open the season, a Leafs record. Anthony Stolarz stopped 20 of 22, Ilya Sorokin 28 of 31. Toronto is 9-14-3, and the Islanders, up two goals in the third at home, managed to make a team that's 1-8-1 in its last 10 look like it had a plan.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

UTA2WPG4Final: UTA 2, WPG 4

Five goals in the first 14 minutes, then one more in the last seven seconds, and Gabriel Vilardi had three of them. Vilardi opened the scoring at 5:11 and put Winnipeg back ahead at 7:26, both off Kyle Connor, with Utah's Andrew Peeke and Lawson Crouse answering each time. Morgan Barron's goal at 14:00 of the first stood as the winner, and Vilardi finished the hat trick into the empty net at 19:53. In between, Utah threw everything at Stuart Skinner, who stopped 34 of 36 while the Jets got 15 shots all night. Sebastian Cossa stopped 11 of 14 for Utah. Winnipeg is 12-9-4 and 8-1-1 in its last 10. Utah is 12-10-3 and 3-4-3 in its last 10. Outshooting a team 36-15 and losing by two is a skill, and the Mammoth have been practicing it.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

ANA2SEA3Final: ANA 2, SEA 3

Forty minutes of nothing, then five goals in the third, and Seattle had the last one. Ben Meyers opened it at 2:51, and Cutter Gauthier answered 75 seconds later for his 22nd of the season and his 18th in November, two shy of the NHL record for a calendar month with three games left in it. Vince Dunn put Seattle back ahead, Sam Colangelo tied it at 12:35, and Kaapo Kakko scored the winner at 17:35 off Brandon Montour and Mackie Samoskevich. Joey Daccord stopped 24 of 26. Lukas Dostal stopped 18 of 21 for Anaheim. The Kraken are 11-9-1. The Ducks have lost four straight and are 11-13-1, which means Gauthier is chasing Teemu Selanne and Joe Malone while the rest of the roster chases Gauthier.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

MIN5SJS2Final: MIN 5, SJS 2

Filip Gustavsson made his season debut after hip surgery, the Wild set a franchise record with a point in a 15th straight game, and Jared Spurgeon passed Mikko Koivu for the most games in Wild history at 1,029. San Jose was mostly there to hold the door. The Sharks did lead 2-1 in the first, on a Tyler Toffoli power-play goal and Alexander Wennberg's first of the season, both set up by Macklin Celebrini. Then Brock Faber tied it with 42 seconds left in the period, and Joel Eriksson Ek scored 13 seconds into the second for the winner. Kirill Kaprizov had a goal and two assists, Eriksson Ek and Blake Coleman added empty-netters, and Gustavsson stopped 22 of 24. Yaroslav Askarov stopped 25 of 28. Minnesota is 18-3-5 with 41 points, the most in the league. San Jose is 11-13-2 and got exactly one period of being a problem.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Monday, November 23

Game recap

CAR5NYR2Final: CAR 5, NYR 2

Carolina walked into Madison Square Garden and did what Carolina does: shot the Rangers into submission, 5-2. Eric Robinson opened it shorthanded in the first, because why bother waiting for your own power play. Mika Zibanejad answered on the Rangers' man advantage 72 seconds later, and that was the last time New York looked like it belonged. The Canes then dropped three in the second inside 5:14: Jackson Blake, Alexander Nikishin and Sean Walker, the kind of stretch that turns a Sunday crowd into a Sunday nap. J.T. Miller scored 6-on-5 on a power play with Dylan Garand pulled, and Jordan Martinook iced it into the empty net. Garand made 36 saves on 40 shots. Brandon Bussi stopped 25 of 27. The Rangers got outshot 40-27 at home, which is a lot of money to pay for a view of the other team's offensive zone.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

BUF6TBL2Final: BUF 6, TBL 2

Tampa came home and Buffalo treated Amalie Arena like a rental it didn't have to return: Sabres 6, Lightning 2. Jiri Kulich scored unassisted 3:35 in, Nikita Kucherov tied it on the power play, and then the Lightning disappeared into the second period like it was a Florida sinkhole. Jack Quinn put Buffalo ahead 1:22 in, and Tage Thompson scored twice, once on the power play and once at even strength, both set up by Zach Benson. Gage Goncalves got his first of the season to make it 4-2, and Noah Ostlund took that hope back exactly one minute later. Benson finished with three points and an empty-netter. Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen stopped 29 of 31, while Dennis Hildeby made 22 saves on 27 shots, an .815 night he'll want to forget. Tampa is used to shutting doors on teams at home; last night Buffalo walked straight through them, and nobody bothered locking up.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

EDM4STL5SOFinal: EDM 4, STL 5 SO

Edmonton led St. Louis 4-1 with less than ten minutes left and still found a way to lose in a shootout, 5-4. Kasperi Kapanen, Leon Draisaitl, Filip Hallander and Colton Dach built the lead, with Dalibor Dvorsky the only Blue to answer through two. Then the third period happened. Philip Broberg scored 6-on-5 at 10:27, Pavel Buchnevich made it 4-3 at 15:12, and Jimmy Snuggerud tied it 26 seconds later. In the shootout Connor McDavid scored, Jake Neighbours answered, Draisaitl missed, Mason McTavish buried his and Owen Michaels couldn't keep it going. Joel Hofer stopped 26 of 30, Tristan Jarry 23 of 27. Evan Bouchard logged 32:25 and the Oilers still couldn't hold on for the last ten minutes. A three-goal lead in the third used to be a sure thing; in Edmonton it's just a head start for the other team.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

PIT0DAL1Final: PIT 0, DAL 1

Pittsburgh and Dallas played a game that looked like a goalie clinic with a skating break in the middle: Stars 1, Penguins 0. The only goal came 12:44 into the second, when Joel Kiviranta finished a play set up by Wyatt Johnston and Mikko Rantanen. Jake Oettinger stopped all 33 shots for the shutout, the kind of night that makes a defense look like it knew what it was doing. Arturs Silovs was nearly as good at the other end, 22 saves on 23 shots, and he got nothing for it but a seat on the bench for an extra attacker that never mattered. Pittsburgh outshot Dallas and still left with zero, which isn't bad luck so much as a pattern: lots of shots, no finish. The Penguins went to Texas looking for a goal and came home carrying an empty bag.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

CHI6VAN3Final: CHI 6, VAN 3

Chicago scored four goals in the first 12:44 in Vancouver and spent the rest of the night collecting souvenirs: Blackhawks 6, Canucks 3. Frank Nazar scored 35 seconds in, Tyler Bertuzzi added a power-play goal, and Roman Kantserov did the rest with a hat trick and four points, two of his goals on the man advantage. Dominic Toninato chipped in his first of the season, which tells you how the first period was going. Zeev Buium, Filip Chytil and Jake DeBrusk scored for Vancouver to make it look like a game for a while. Patrick Kane had two assists. Drew Commesso stopped 22 of 25. Nikita Tolopilo stopped 7 of 11 and was gone by 12:44 of the first; Kevin Lankinen came on and made 17 saves on 19 shots. Vancouver's penalty kill gave up three goals at home to Chicago, and that's a sentence nobody in B.C. wanted to read.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Sunday, November 22

Game recap

EDM4CAR7Final: EDM 4, CAR 7

Edmonton led 3-1 in Raleigh, which in Oilers terms is the part of the horror movie where somebody says they'll be right back. Owen Michaels, Leon Draisaitl (his 22nd, on the power play) and a shorthanded Mathieu Joseph built the lead, and then Carolina scored six of the next seven. Jalen Chatfield, Taylor Hall and Andrei Svechnikov struck in a 3:05 stretch of the second, Sebastian Aho put the Hurricanes ahead for good on the power play with 26 seconds left in the period, and Svechnikov and Alexander Nikishin finished it. Carolina scored three power-play goals, and Aho had a goal and two assists. Pyotr Kochetkov won while stopping 11 of 15, a save percentage usually reserved for beer league. Devon Levi faced 36 shots and a penalty kill that kills nothing but Edmonton's evenings.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

CHI4CGY3OTFinal: CHI 4, CGY 3 OT

Dillon Boucher and Adam Klapka dropped the gloves four seconds in, which turned out to be the most organized thing Calgary did all night. Ryan Strome gave the Flames the lead, then Chicago scored three times in 3:05 of the second: Roman Kantserov's 10th, Ryan Donato with the extra attacker on and Patrick Kane on the power play. Calgary clawed back through Jonathan Castagna and a Yegor Sharangovich power-play goal early in the third, but Sam Rinzel ended it at 4:45 of overtime, his third point of the night. Kane, who apparently plans to do this until the sun burns out, had a goal and two assists. Spencer Knight stopped 33 of 36; Dustin Wolf stopped 29 of 33 and deserved a better cause. The Flames got a point, which is what Calgary calls a moral victory and the standings call 3-on-3 charity.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

BUF3FLA4Final: BUF 3, FLA 4

Sam Bennett spent Saturday treating the Sabres like a rental car. He scored three minutes in, answered Jack Quinn's go-ahead goal 18 seconds later, and put Florida in front shorthanded 48 seconds into the third for the hat trick, his eighth, ninth and 10th of the season. Buffalo, to its credit, kept getting up: Jiri Kulich, Quinn and Tage Thompson (his 15th) each tied or led. So Bennett went and set up Sandis Vilmanis for the winner with 3:18 left, a four-point night. Jacob Markstrom needed only 16 saves on 19 shots. Alex Lyon stopped 26 of 30 and is 0-3-1 since coming back, and Lindy Ruff said his team got beat at the net front on the winner. The Sabres are 9-10-4, a record that looks exactly like every Sabres record you have ever seen.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

PIT3NSH4Final: PIT 3, NSH 4

The Penguins led 2-0 in Nashville, and Andrei Kuzmenko, a healthy scratch in five of the previous six games, scored his first goal in black and gold. That was the good part, and it lasted about 70 seconds. Jonathan Marchessault got one back before the first period ended, Filip Forsberg and Reid Schaefer scored in the first 6:22 of the second, and after Hendrix Lapierre tied it at 3, Jayden Struble won it 3:31 into the third off feeds from Steven Stamkos and Ryan O'Reilly. Marchessault and Brady Skjei had two points each, Juuse Saros stopped 21 of 24, and Sergei Murashov made 25 saves in the loss. Samuel Girard had the other Pittsburgh goal with Tommy Novak in the top-line seat beside Sidney Crosby. Ottawa's general manager watched from the press box, and the Penguins played like a team that knew the store was open.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

WSH5BOS7Final: WSH 5, BOS 7

Elias Lindholm scored four goals, and at no point did anyone in a Capitals sweater seem interested in finding out where he was standing. He scored on the power play in the first, twice in the second and again 4:07 into the third, and set up David Pastrnak in between for a five-point night. Morgan Geekie had three assists, Tanner Jeannot scored, and even Jeremy Swayman picked up an assist while stopping 30 of 35. Washington kept it a game: Tom Wilson, a shorthanded Alex Tuch, Pierre-Luc Dubois and Dylan Strome had it tied 4-4 in the second, and Jakob Chychrun made it 6-5 late before Fraser Minten hit the empty net. Charlie Lindgren allowed six on 22 shots. That's five straight losses and a sub-.500 record for the Capitals, and Spencer Carbery said that if you cannot defend in this league, you will never win. Seven goals against is a strong supporting argument.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

CBJ4TOR3Final: CBJ 4, TOR 3

The Maple Leafs led 3-1 at home and lost, because of course they did, and because the hockey gods have a sense of humor the winning rally ran through Matthew Knies, the winger Toronto traded to Columbus in September. Auston Matthews (his 14th, on the power play), Jake McCabe and Teddy Blueger built the lead. Knies set up Adam Fantilli's power-play goal in the second, tied it himself, unassisted, with 4:20 left, and 52 seconds later Zach Werenski scored the winner from Fantilli. Cam Talbot made 23 saves; Anthony Stolarz stopped 31 of 35 and has seen this movie. That's nine straight losses, 0-8-1, for an 8-14-3 team whose coach, Jim Hiller, called the night just not National Hockey League level. Toronto has spent decades finding new ways to lose. Getting beat by its own trade is at least efficient.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

PHI4MTL3Final: PHI 4, MTL 3

Montreal spent the third period erasing a two-goal deficit and the last 31 seconds finding out none of it mattered. Noah Cates scored at 19:29, from Sean Couturier and Matvei Michkov, and the Flyers walked out of the Bell Centre with both points and most of the building's good mood. Christian Dvorak opened the scoring, Oliver Kapanen answered 16 seconds later, and Denver Barkey (a goal and an assist) and Rasmus Ristolainen made it 3-1 in the second, both set up by Owen Tippett. Zachary Bolduc on the power play and Owen Beck tied it 74 seconds apart early in the third. Dan Vladar stopped 20 of 23. Jacob Fowler saw 20 shots and four of them went in, which is a rough way to spend a Saturday night in front of 21,000 amateur goalie coaches. The Canadiens did the hard part and then forgot the easy part: the last half-minute.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

LAK2OTT4Final: LAK 2, OTT 4

For most of two periods the Kings led 1-0 on a Mats Zuccarello goal and played the kind of hockey that makes you check your phone. Then Nick Cousins tied it with 54 seconds left in the second, and Tim Stützle decided the third period was his. He scored 30 seconds in, set up Stephen Halliday's power-play goal at 5:54 and scored again at 7:16: three Ottawa goals in 6:46, three points for Stützle, his 12th and 13th of the season. Dylan Cozens and Jake Sanderson had two assists each. Linus Ullmark stopped 19 of 21 and was mostly asked to stay awake. Anton Forsberg made 24 saves, and Quinton Byfield's late goal made the score look friendlier than the period was. Los Angeles held a lead for two periods and had no idea what to do with it, the same way it handles the first round.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

NYI3DET2Final: NYI 3, DET 2

Ondrej Palat came into the night with two goals all season and left Detroit with four, which tells you what kind of evening the Red Wings had. Emmitt Finnie put Detroit up in the first, Palat tied it in the second, Simon Holmstrom scored his 10th early in the third to stretch his point streak to seven games, and Palat's second made it 3-1. Alex DeBrincat answered 29 seconds later, and that was all. Matthew Schaefer had two assists and now has 85 career points, passing Rasmus Dahlin for the second most by a teenage defenseman; only Phil Housley had more. Ilya Sorokin stopped 18 of 20, John Gibson 18 of 21, and Ben Chiarot and Brayden Schenn fought late in the second for the purists. The Islanders have points in seven straight. Detroit managed 20 shots at home, a rebuild now old enough to ask for the car keys.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

NJD6STL9Final: NJD 6, STL 9

Fifteen goals in St. Louis, and somewhere a goalie coach is updating his resume. The Blues led 3-0 before six minutes were gone on goals from Brandon Carlo, Jimmy Snuggerud (his 13th, on the power play) and Robert Thomas, and when Philip Broberg made it 4-1 at 9:03, Connor Hellebuyck's night was over: four goals on six shots. Jake Allen came in and gave up four more. Jake Neighbours had five assists, the kind of line you normally need a video game to produce, and Broberg, Thomas and Logan Mailloux each had a goal and two assists. New Jersey never went away, getting within one twice on goals from Timo Meier, Luke Hughes and Connor Brown, but Pavel Buchnevich, Mailloux, Mason McTavish and Jonatan Berggren (twice, one into the empty net) kept answering. Jordan Binnington allowed six on 43 shots and won comfortably. The Devils scored six and lost by three, which is less a hockey game than a cry for help.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

VGK5WPG4SOFinal: VGK 5, WPG 4 SO

Adam Lowry scored 29 seconds in and the Jets still found a way to hand out a souvenir point and keep none of the good ones. Vegas answered through Brett Howden and Mitch Marner, Viggo Björck tied it before the first intermission, and the teams traded from there: Tomas Hertl's 10th on the power play, Mark Scheifele, then Kyle Connor's 19th to put Winnipeg up 4-3 early in the third. Ivan Barbashev tied it with 3:35 left, and in the shootout William Karlsson scored the only goal while Carter Hart turned away Scheifele, Connor and Gabriel Vilardi. Jack Eichel had two assists, Hertl and Howden a goal and an assist each. Hart stopped 26 of 30; Stuart Skinner made 29 saves and lost anyway. Winnipeg led twice at home and went 0-for-3 in the skills contest, proof that you can change the goalie and keep the ending.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

ANA2UTA3Final: ANA 2, UTA 3

Utah won a hockey game with 12 shots on goal, the first NHL team to win with that few since the Rangers in March 2025, and one of the 12 went into an empty net. Call it efficiency. Leo Carlsson opened the scoring for Anaheim, Vincent Trocheck tied it unassisted, and Andrew Peeke put the Mammoth ahead in the second from Logan Cooley and Daniil But. Cooley's empty-netter with 1:17 left, his 12th, ended up as the winner when Ian Moore scored with 12 seconds to go. In between, Sebastian Cossa stopped 29 of 31 while his teammates took the night off in front of him, and Utah did it without Clayton Keller, a late scratch with an illness. The Mammoth are 12-9-3. The Ducks outshot a team 31-12 and lost, which takes a level of commitment to disappointment that Anaheim has been perfecting for years.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

MIN3VAN4SOFinal: MIN 3, VAN 4 SO

Marco Rossi hadn't scored in 21 games, so naturally he scored twice against Minnesota, the second with the goalie pulled and 1:23 left, 35 seconds after Nick Foligno looked like he'd won it for the Wild. Luke Schenn and Marcus Foligno fought two minutes in to set the mood. Matt Boldy (his 14th) and Jared Spurgeon scored for Minnesota, both set up by Kirill Kaprizov, whose 14-game point streak ties the franchise record; the Wild have points in 14 straight themselves. Rossi on the power play and Zeev Buium, with his first of the season, kept Vancouver level, and Brock Boeser assisted on three goals to push his point streak to a career-high 10 games. Jake DeBrusk had the only goal of the shootout, and Leevi Meriläinen, 22 saves on 25 shots, stopped Maxim Shabanov, Boldy and Kaprizov. Jesper Wallstedt made 21 saves. Minnesota was 83 seconds from two points and settled for one, plus a reminder from a guy who used to wear the sweater.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

SEA3SJS4Final: SEA 3, SJS 4

Kaapo Kakko scored on the power play to put Seattle ahead, and the Kraken enjoyed that lead for all of 29 seconds. Michael Misa tied it, Nolan Allan put San Jose in front, and Macklin Celebrini (his 10th) and Ivar Stenberg added power-play goals to make it 4-1 before the game was half over. Dmitry Orlov assisted on three of the four, and Celebrini and Stenberg, a goal and an assist apiece, look like a problem the Pacific Division will be filing complaints about for a decade. Seattle made it interesting with second-period goals from Matty Beniers and Ryan Winterton, then spent the third finding out Alex Nedeljkovic was done giving: 27 saves on 30 shots. Philipp Grubauer stopped 25 of 29. The Kraken took the penalties, the Sharks took the points, and Seattle remains the league's most reliably forgettable way to spend a Saturday night.

Friday, November 20

Game recap

LAK4TOR3SOFinal: LAK 4, TOR 3 SO

Up 3-0 at home with a franchise record already in the books, the Maple Leafs had this one gift-wrapped, and then did what the Maple Leafs do with gifts. Auston Matthews opened the scoring on the power play, his 68th game-opening goal, passing Mats Sundin for the team record, John Tavares made it two, and Dakota Joshua's first of the season made it three early in the second. The lead lasted 21 seconds before Alex Turcotte answered, Alex Laferriere scored on the power play, and Erik Haula tied it before the second period was over. Two fights two seconds apart in the first (Duhaime and Perry, Blueger and Laughton) turned out to be Toronto's last signs of life. Adrian Kempe had the only goal of the shootout, Darcy Kuemper stopped 24 of 27 plus all three shooters, and Anthony Stolarz's 25 saves went to waste. That's eight straight losses for Toronto, a team that can now turn a three-goal lead into a moral victory faster than you can say 1967.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

PHI6OTT5OTFinal: PHI 6, OTT 5 OT

Ottawa led 5-2 with under 15 minutes to play and still found a way to hand out two points like Halloween candy. Dylan Cozens scored twice, Drake Batherson had a goal and an assist, Tim Stützle set up two, and when Cozens made it 5-2 at 5:27 of the third the building was ready to go home happy. Then Cam York scored his second of the night on the power play, Tyson Foerster scored 15 seconds later, and Jamie Drysdale tied it with the goalie pulled and 2:33 left. Travis Konecny, who had three assists already, needed all of 39 seconds of overtime to finish it, with Joseph Woll picking up an assist to go with his 21 saves on 26 shots. Samuel Ersson stopped 13 of 19, which is a tough way to protect a three-goal lead. The Senators didn't blow a lead so much as leave it on the curb with a free sign.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

STL5PIT2Final: STL 5, PIT 2

Pittsburgh scored first, put 33 shots on net and got a milestone from Evgeni Malkin, and all it bought was a 5-2 loss on home ice. Rickard Rakell opened the scoring in the first, then the Blues took the second period and never gave it back: Justin Barron tied it unassisted, Dylan Holloway put them ahead, and Jimmy Snuggerud scored late in the second and again in the third, his 11th and 12th, both set up by Robert Thomas and Jake Neighbours. Thomas finished with three assists. Rakell got his second with the goalie pulled, on helpers from Sidney Crosby and Malkin, whose 1,425th point tied Bryan Trottier for 19th in NHL history, before Holloway's empty-netter closed it. Joel Hofer stopped 31 of 33; Arturs Silovs stopped 28 of 32. The Penguins keep collecting history like it's a retirement plan, and the standings keep reminding them it isn't one.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

BUF6WSH3Final: BUF 6, WSH 3

Tom Wilson and Sam Carrick dropped the gloves one second into the game, and that was the last fight Washington put up for a while. Buffalo scored three times on its first five shots, with Jack Quinn, Rasmus Dahlin on the power play and Beck Malenstyn chasing Logan Thompson after 10 minutes and 11 seconds of work. Alex Tuch answered unassisted, Zach Benson made it 4-1 before the intermission, and Tage Thompson's 14th, a power-play goal with nine seconds left in the second, made it five. Ryan Leonard and Boone Jenner scored 52 seconds apart in the third to make it interesting, with Alex Ovechkin's assist on Jenner's goal his 763rd, a Capitals record, but Quinn's empty-netter gave him two goals and three points. Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen stopped 34 of 37 as the Sabres ended a five-game skid. Ovechkin's goal drought is at 15 games, the longest of his career, and the Capitals' goaltending just had a drought of its own: about ten minutes without a save anyone remembers.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

MTL2CAR1OTFinal: MTL 2, CAR 1 OT

For 53 minutes this was a goalie clinic nobody asked to attend, and then Lane Hutson decided he had somewhere to be. Nikolaj Ehlers finally broke the scoreless tie with 6:19 left in the third, and Carolina, a team built to sit on a one-goal lead like it's a family heirloom, held it for exactly 80 seconds. Hutson tied it from Nick Suzuki and Cole Caufield, then won it 38 seconds into overtime, with Suzuki setting up both. Jakub Dobes stopped 26 of 27 for Montreal; Pyotr Kochetkov stopped 22 of 24 and had his four-game win streak end anyway. Taylor Hall and Kaiden Guhle fought in the third, which for a long stretch was the only thing on the scoresheet worth reading. The Hurricanes outshot a team, led late and lost it in overtime, which is less a result than a franchise tradition.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

NYI3WPG4OTFinal: NYI 3, WPG 4 OT

The Islanders led three separate times in Winnipeg and went home with one point, the hockey version of winning every round and losing the fight. Anthony Duclair scored 2:35 in and Morgan Barron answered 31 seconds later. Emil Heineman scored shorthanded and Kyle Connor tied it with his 18th. Kyle Palmieri scored 20 seconds into the second and Cole Perfetti tied it on the power play. Then nobody scored for nearly 50 minutes, apparently out of exhaustion, until Josh Morrissey picked the 1:58 mark of overtime for his first goal of the season. Mark Scheifele had three assists, Connor and Gabriel Vilardi had two points each, and Nico Daws stopped 22 of 25 for the Jets, who have won seven of eight. Semyon Varlamov stopped 18 of 22. New York's point streak is at six games, which sounds great until you notice how many of those leads it took to get one point out of this one.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

EDM1TBL3Final: EDM 1, TBL 3

Connor McDavid had a point in every game this season, all 23 of them, until Andrei Vasilevskiy decided the streak had gone on long enough. The Lightning goalie stopped 23 of 24 and was 96 seconds from a shutout when Colton Dach finally got one past him. By then it was over. John Carlson opened the scoring on a second-period power play, set up by Jake Guentzel and Brayden Point, Ilya Mikheyev made it 2-0 midway through the third, and Nikita Kucherov added an unassisted goal four minutes later. Devon Levi stopped 17 of 19 and deserved better than a team that put 24 shots on net and waited 58 minutes to make one count. Edmonton without McDavid on the scoresheet turns out to be exactly what everyone suspected: a very expensive group of people watching Vasilevskiy play goal.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

CBJ4CHI2Final: CBJ 4, CHI 2

Rick Bowness came back to the Columbus bench and the Blue Jackets remembered how to win, ending a five-game losing streak in the one building where that's easiest to arrange. Zach Werenski scored 1:59 in and set up Kent Johnson's ninth later in the first, and both finished with a goal and an assist. Frank Nazar got Chicago on the board with a power-play goal, his 11th, and Matthew Knies answered with a power-play goal of his own two minutes later. Cole Smith made it 3-2 early in the third, but Cam Talbot stopped 23 of 25 and Adam Fantilli hit the empty net with 31 seconds left, giving Knies a three-point night. Spencer Knight stopped 29 of 32. The Blackhawks played without Connor Bedard and it looked like it: 25 shots, two goals, and a rebuild that's starting to qualify for historic-landmark status.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

MIN4CGY1Final: MIN 4, CGY 1

The Wild scored 25 seconds in, and Calgary spent the other 59:35 confirming that was a fair summary of the evening. Joel Eriksson Ek opened it from Matt Boldy and Kirill Kaprizov, Quinn Hughes made it 2-0 eight minutes later, and after Simon Nemec got one back for the Flames, Kaprizov's 18th of the season, on the power play, restored the two-goal lead early in the second. Boldy hit the empty net late for a goal and two assists; Kaprizov had the same line and Hughes and Eriksson Ek each had a goal and an assist. Jesper Wallstedt stopped 22 of 23, Dustin Wolf stopped 18 of 21, and Ryan Hartman and Martin Pospisil fought with one second left in the first, the closest Calgary came to landing anything. That's five straight wins and a 13-game point streak for Minnesota. The Flames, meanwhile, are the red carpet other teams' streaks walk in on.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

ANA0COL4Final: ANA 0, COL 4

Cutter Gauthier walked into Denver with goals in 10 straight games and walked out with a participation ribbon, like every other Duck. Scott Wedgewood stopped all 25 shots for the shutout, and Colorado did its damage in one period: Nicolas Roy scored eight seconds into the second, Brock Nelson added a power-play goal at 3:25 and another at even strength at 10:04, and that was that. Devon Toews made it 4-0 in the third, finishing with a goal and an assist, while Nelson had two goals and an assist and Martin Necas set up two. Lukas Dostal stopped 23 of 27 and can file a complaint with the 18 skaters in front of him. Anaheim's night lasted 20 scoreless minutes and then eight seconds; after that it was just altitude sickness with a scoreboard.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

VAN1SEA5Final: VAN 1, SEA 5

Berkly Catton picked a fine night for his first NHL hat trick, mostly because Vancouver picked a fine night to stop defending. The Kraken rookie opened the scoring on the power play, scored unassisted in the second 54 seconds after Matty Beniers had broken a 1-1 tie, and finished it into an empty net with 43 seconds left for his eighth of the season. Jordan Eberle added a power-play goal, and Beniers and Brandon Montour each had two points. Jake DeBrusk's power-play goal was all the Canucks got past Philipp Grubauer, who stopped 22 of 23. The real story was at the other end: Seattle put 42 shots on Leevi Meriläinen, who made 38 saves and got a 5-1 loss for his trouble. Vancouver gave its goalie a 42-shot workload and one goal of support, which isn't a game plan so much as a hostage situation.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

DAL4VGK3SOFinal: DAL 4, VGK 3 SO

Mark Stone set the Golden Knights' all-time points record with No. 418, and Dallas made sure the party ended with someone else blowing out the candles. Miro Heiskanen and Wyatt Johnston had the Stars up 2-0 after one, both set up by Jason Robertson, before Vegas ran off three straight: Victor Olofsson on the power play, with Stone's record-setting assist, William Karlsson, and Jeremy Lauzon's first of the season early in the third. That lead held until Thomas Harley tied it unassisted with 3:02 left in regulation. In the shootout, Robertson and Tyler Seguin both scored, Trevor Connelly had the only Vegas goal, and Jake Oettinger stopped Braeden Bowman to end it. Oettinger made 27 saves on 30 shots; Adin Hill stopped 19 of 22. Vegas outshot Dallas 30-22, held a third-period lead at home and lost a coin flip, the kind of hospitality the Strip usually reserves for tourists.

Thursday, November 19

Game recap

BOS4DET1Final: BOS 4, DET 1

Detroit threw itself a 100th birthday party and Boston ate the cake. The Red Wings' Centennial Celebration Game started on script, Lucas Raymond scoring his ninth late in the first, and then the Bruins scored the next four like guests who found the open bar. JJ Peterka tied it early in the second, Pavel Zacha put Boston ahead on the power play, David Pastrnak buried his 10th in the third and Casey Mittelstadt hit the empty net, with Zacha, Pastrnak and Mittelstadt each adding an assist. Mason Lohrei and Morgan Geekie had two helpers apiece. Jeremy Swayman, on the second night of a back-to-back, stopped 20 of 21, which is less a workload than a light jog. Daniil Tarasov made 27 saves on 30 shots and deserved a better party. Boston's three-game skid is over, 4-1. Detroit has a century of history and one goal to show for the night: the franchise turned 100, and the offense skated like it.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

MTL3NJD2Final: MTL 3, NJD 2

Lane Hutson didn't score and still ran the building. The Canadiens defenseman set up all three Montreal goals in a 3-2 win in Newark, handing Connor Hellebuyck his first loss as a Devil. The first period was a track meet: Luke Evangelista opened the scoring, Alex Newhook answered 40 seconds later, Timo Meier put New Jersey back in front, and Nick Suzuki tied it on the power play with 42 seconds left before the break. Then everybody remembered defense existed, until Jake Evans scored the winner 6:17 into the third. Jacob Fowler stopped 28 of 30 for Montreal; Hellebuyck stopped 25 of 28. Jack Hughes fired four shots, won a quarter of his faceoffs and went home with nothing. The Devils finally have their goalie in the crease, and the skaters picked that night to take one off. That's New Jersey for you: fix the roof, leave the windows open.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

COL1UTA4Final: COL 1, UTA 4

Utah's six-game winless streak died the way hockey intended: a fourth-liner's goal and a fistfight four seconds later. Liam O'Brien scored his first of the season 5:22 into the second, Jack McBain and Gabriel Landeskog dropped the gloves before the goal was announced, and the Mammoth rolled to a 4-1 win. Vincent Trocheck added a power-play goal late in the period, O'Brien celebrated by fighting Alex Gagne 38 seconds after that, and Trocheck set up Dmitri Simashev shorthanded a minute into the third. Sebastian Cossa stopped 30 of 31, losing the shutout to Jaden Schwartz with five minutes left, and Kevin Stenlund hit the empty net. Mackenzie Blackwood made 25 saves on 28 shots. Colorado gave up goals at even strength, on the penalty kill and on its own power play. That's not a loss, that's a sampler platter.

Wednesday, November 18

Game recap

LAK3BOS0Final: LAK 3, BOS 0

Darcy Kuemper walked into TD Garden, stopped all 29 shots for his 40th career shutout, then picked up an assist on the empty-netter, which means the Kings' goalie outscored the entire Bruins roster. Mats Zuccarello opened the scoring late in the first off a feed from Erik Gustafsson, who was back after three games out. Andre Lee made it 2-0 late in the second, and Gustafsson finished it into the empty net with Kuemper getting the helper. Los Angeles ends a four-game losing streak. Michael DiPietro did his part, 19 saves on 21, and got the run support of a man jogging alone. Marco Sturm reunited David Pastrnak, Elias Lindholm and Morgan Geekie, and the reunion tour sold zero tickets. That's three straight losses for Boston, which now heads to Detroit's centennial party as the guest who forgot to bring a gift, or a goal.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

EDM5FLA2Final: EDM 5, FLA 2

Connor McDavid ran his point streak to 23 games and passed Wayne Gretzky for the Oilers' record in power-play points along the way, the kind of sentence you only get to write about one guy. Edmonton was up 4-0 before Florida found the building: Kasperi Kapanen opened it, McDavid scored on the power play, and Vasily Podkolzin scored twice in the second, his 11th and 12th, one of them on the power play too. Podkolzin, Kapanen and Leon Draisaitl all finished with three points. Matthew Tkachuk scored twice in the last seven minutes to push his own point streak to nine games, and Draisaitl's 21st into the empty net ended the suspense. Devon Levi stopped 20 of 22. Jacob Markstrom stopped 13 of 17, a .765 that plays as a batting average and nowhere else. The Panthers took almost 54 minutes to show up to their own home game, which in South Florida still counts as early.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

CBJ1NYI5Final: CBJ 1, NYI 5

Matthew Schaefer scored his first career hat trick, the first by an Islanders defenseman since Denis Potvin in 1982, and when the comparison is Potvin you can stop the scouting report there. He scored unassisted early in the second for a 2-0 lead, restored the two-goal cushion in the third after Zach Werenski had cut it to 2-1, and finished into the empty net, his ninth of the season on nine shots on goal for the night. Anthony Duclair opened the scoring on a power play with 58 seconds left in the first, Tony DeAngelo added one, Mathew Barzal had two assists, and Ilya Sorokin stopped 28 of 29. Cam Talbot faced 40 shots, stopped 36 and should file for hazard pay. That's five straight regulation losses for Columbus. The Blue Jackets have finally found consistency. It's just the wrong kind.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

BUF3PHI4Final: BUF 3, PHI 4

The Sabres led 47 seconds in, led again midway through the second, and lost anyway, because Buffalo handles a lead like a hot pan. Mattias Samuelsson opened the scoring, Jamie Drysdale tied it, Tage Thompson's 13th put Buffalo back in front, and Owen Tippett tied it again. Travis Sanheim gave Philadelphia its first lead 29 seconds into the third, Jiri Kulich answered with his first goal in 11 games, and Christian Dvorak won it 52 seconds after that. Matvei Michkov's two assists stretched his point streak to five games. Nobody is framing the goalie lines: Joseph Woll stopped 16 of 19 and won, Alex Lyon stopped 29 of 33 and didn't. Outshot 33-19 and still tied in the third, the Sabres found the most Buffalo way to get nothing. Five straight losses, and it's mid-November with fans already checking the lottery odds, the one annual tradition this franchise never misses.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

OTT2WPG1Final: OTT 2, WPG 1

Tyler Boucher, the 10th overall pick in 2021, waited five years for his first NHL game and then scored the winner in it, which is one way to make up for lost time. Ottawa got both of its goals 58 seconds apart early in the second: Drake Batherson's 11th on the power play, then Boucher off a pass from Thomas Chabot. Winnipeg's Viggo Björck answered with his own first NHL goal five minutes later, and that was the end of the scoring, with more than half the game still to play. Linus Ullmark stopped 20 of 21. Stuart Skinner stopped 25 of 27 and got a loss for his trouble. The Senators have won three straight, and the Jets' six-game winning streak is over. Winnipeg had a heater on the line at home and put 21 shots on net, the offensive urgency of a team returning a library book.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

WSH2TBL5Final: WSH 2, TBL 5

Tampa Bay got Brayden Point, Anthony Cirelli and Erik Cernak back in the lineup and had a 3-0 lead before the Capitals finished stretching. Sam O'Reilly scored his first NHL goal 2:11 in, with Point picking up an assist, Charle-Edouard D'Astous made it two, and Jake Guentzel made it three at 13:11. Alex Tuch got one back, Guentzel scored again in the second for his 13th, Ryan Leonard made it 4-2 in the third, and Cirelli closed it into the empty net. John Carlson had three assists against his old team, because of course he did, and Nikita Kucherov had two in his 900th game. Andrei Vasilevskiy stopped 25 of 27; Logan Thompson stopped 20 of 24. Washington has lost three straight for the first time this season, and Alex Ovechkin's goal drought is at 14 games, tying the longest of his career. The man caught Gretzky. Right now he can't catch a break, a bounce or a Tuesday in Tampa.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

TOR3CHI6Final: TOR 3, CHI 6

Make it seven straight losses for the Maple Leafs, and this one came with a former Leaf doing the honors. Easton Cowan put Toronto up 3:22 in, and then the second period got silly: Frank Nazar scored twice, Teddy Blueger tied it 22 seconds after Nazar's second, and Connor Bedard put Chicago ahead for good 35 seconds after that. Tyler Bertuzzi made it 4-2 on a third-period power play, John Tavares cut it to one, and the Blackhawks answered in 12 seconds through Oliver Moore, then again 49 seconds later on Bertuzzi's second of the night. Sam Rinzel had three assists. Spencer Knight stopped 31 of 34; Sergei Bobrovsky stopped 19 of 25, a .760 that explains plenty. Toronto outshot Chicago 34-25 and lost by three. The Leafs have found the one thing harder to watch than their Aprils: their Novembers.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

ANA6STL8Final: ANA 6, STL 8

Fourteen goals, eight different Blues scorers, one Cutter Gauthier hat trick, and a final two minutes that should come with a seat belt. Gauthier scored his 19th, 20th and 21st to run his goal streak to 10 games, one short of Teemu Selanne's Ducks record, added an assist, and lost in regulation. St. Louis broke it open with three goals in 2:58 of the third, from Jake Neighbours, Philip Broberg and Logan Mailloux, whose first of the season capped a career-high three-point night. That made it 7-3 and ended Ville Husso's evening at seven goals on 24 shots. Anaheim then scored three straight, two with the net empty, to get within 7-6 with 41 seconds left, and Pavel Buchnevich hit the empty net three seconds later. Jordan Binnington allowed six on 31 in his first start since Nov. 5 and won comfortably, sort of. The Ducks scored six and never led. Defense in this one was a rumor nobody could confirm.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

NSH3MIN7Final: NSH 3, MIN 7

The Wild's point streak is at 12 games, and the Predators were kind enough to settle this one before the first intermission. Brock Faber scored his first of the season 4:20 in, Blake Coleman and Maxim Shabanov followed, and Matt Boldy made it 4-0 with 81 seconds left in the period, then 5-0 on the power play 59 seconds into the second. Nicolas Hague got Nashville on the board, Marcus Foligno answered 17 seconds later off a pass from brother Nick, and that was it for Justus Annunen: six goals on 20 shots. Juuse Saros stopped 17 of 18 in relief, a nice effort for a game already in the trash. Joel Eriksson Ek had a goal and three assists, Kirill Kaprizov had three assists, and Jesper Wallstedt stopped 25 of 28. Jonathan Marchessault scored in his return for Nashville, whose road trip ended like a bad night on Broadway: early, loud and with somebody getting pulled out of there.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

DAL4VGK3OTFinal: DAL 4, VGK 3 OT

Vegas led 3-1 with 78 seconds left and lost, a collapse so fast the building didn't have time to boo it properly. William Karlsson scored twice and Brett Howden added a third, and the Golden Knights were a minute and change from ending their skid. Then Dallas pulled Jake Oettinger: Wyatt Johnston scored at 18:42, Mikko Rantanen tied it with five seconds on the clock, and Miro Heiskanen, in his first game back after missing five, won it 3:36 into overtime. Rantanen had a goal and three assists, a point on every Stars goal, including Nils Lundkvist's first of the season. Oettinger stopped 24 of 27; Adin Hill stopped 18 of 22. That's three straight losses for Vegas, and the same two teams go again Thursday in the same building. The Knights had this one counted, cashed and halfway to the cage, then learned what every tourist on the Strip already knows: you're not up until you walk out the door.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

CGY5SJS2Final: CGY 5, SJS 2

Jonathan Castagna showed up in San Jose without an NHL goal and left with two, and Simon Nemec scored his first as a Flame, so Calgary's equipment staff spent the night taping pucks. Adam Gaudette put the Sharks up 3:53 in, Matt Coronato tied it 76 seconds later, and Martin Pospisil gave Calgary the lead with 38 seconds left in the first. Nemec's power-play goal early in the second made it 3-1, and Castagna's first made it 4-1 in the third, with an assist to Maxim Tsyplakov in his first game after seven straight in the press box. Mason Marchment scored with the San Jose net empty and a power play going, and Castagna answered into the same empty net. Dustin Wolf stopped 21 of 23; Yaroslav Askarov stopped 24 of 28. The Sharks' future remains bright, mostly because it keeps getting pushed further away.

Tuesday, November 17

Game recap

MTL1NYR3Final: MTL 1, NYR 3

The Rangers threw themselves a centennial party at the Garden and Will Cuylle showed up as both the DJ and the bouncer. Montreal actually scored first, Phillip Danault finishing a Lane Hutson and Noah Dobson setup midway through the second, and that lead lasted a whole 1:48 before Cuylle tied it. Then, with 57 seconds left in the period and the Canadiens on a power play, Cuylle scored again, shorthanded, off an Adam Fox feed, which is the hockey version of getting robbed in your own driveway. Scott Morrow added his first of the season in the third, and Joonas Korpisalo did the rest with 24 saves on 25 shots. Jacob Fowler stopped 23 of 26 and deserved a better night. That's three straight wins for New York and two straight losses for Montreal, whose power play just turned a Rangers birthday party into a gift exchange.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

VAN3UTA2Final: VAN 3, UTA 2

Lock the doors, the Canucks have a winning streak. Two whole games. Nikita Tolopilo made his season debut and treated Utah's 36 shots like spam calls, stopping 34 of them, while Vancouver needed only 24 shots of its own to steal a 3-2 win in Salt Lake City. Brock Boeser ran the show with a goal and two assists: he set up Jake DeBrusk's power-play opener, fed Filip Chytil for a 2-1 lead, then buried the winner himself on another power play with 4:23 left. Utah tied it twice in the third, on Vincent Trocheck's power-play goal and Barrett Hayton's equalizer, and Logan Cooley picked up an assist in his return. None of it mattered. Karel Vejmelka gave up three on 24, and the Mammoth are now six games without a win, the last of them to the team in the league's basement. Extinction usually takes longer than this.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Monday, November 16

Game recap

EDM5PHI2Final: EDM 5, PHI 2

The Oilers went to Philadelphia and treated it like a layover. Edmonton won 5-2, scored twice on the power play in the first and led 3-0 after one, with Leon Draisaitl scoring on the first power play and Vasily Podkolzin, unassisted, on the second. Zach Hyman made it 3-0 for his 500th career point. Cole Knuble and Noah Cates got Philly back within 3-2 in the second, and for one intermission it looked like a game. Then Draisaitl scored 1:07 into the third for his 20th goal, and Connor McDavid put the empty-netter away to finish with a goal and two assists and stretch his point streak to 22 games. Tristan Jarry stopped 34 of 36; Dan Vladar stopped 16 of 19. Edmonton is 9-0-1 on the road. The Flyers are still scoring 2.30 goals a game, the fewest in the league, an offense that's been saving its goals like they're for a rainy day.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

FLA1DAL2OTFinal: FLA 1, DAL 2 OT

Florida and Dallas combined for three goals in 63 minutes, and the Stars got the last one. Matthew Tkachuk opened the scoring on a second-period power play for his 700th career point, then Wyatt Johnston tied it under five minutes later. That was it until overtime, when Jason Robertson finished a Roope Hintz feed at 2:56 for his 10th of the year and a 2-1 Stars win. Casey DeSmith stopped 25 of 26 and Akira Schmid 20 of 22. Thomas Harley played 30:54 with Miro Heiskanen out a fifth straight game, which is less a shift pattern than a hostage situation. Brady Tkachuk threw 10 hits and Colin Blackwell matched him, so plenty of people got hit and almost nobody scored. Florida took a point on the second night of a back-to-back and is 2-0-1 this week, but a power play goal and nothing after it is the kind of night that has the Panthers counting the days until Barkov's back.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

CGY1ANA6Final: CGY 1, ANA 6

Calgary won in Los Angeles on Saturday and then spent Sunday paying for it in Anaheim, 6-1. Jeff Malott scored 1:16 in, and Cutter Gauthier made it 2-0 later in the first, which means he has now scored in nine straight games, the NHL's longest streak in 29 years and two short of Teemu Selanne's Ducks record. Beckett Sennecke had two goals and an assist, one of them into an empty net, Mikael Granlund added a goal and an assist, and Tim Washe scored too. Mikael Backlund's goal early in the third made it 3-1 for all of 25 seconds before Sennecke answered. Ian Moore got an assist in his season debut. Ville Husso stopped 20 of 21, and Devin Cooley, on the second night of a back-to-back, stopped 28 of 33. The Flames are -23 on the season, a goal differential that reads less like a stat and more like a cry for help.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

VAN6VGK3Final: VAN 6, VGK 3

The last-place Canucks walked into T-Mobile Arena and won 6-3, which is the kind of upset Vegas usually charges admission for. Elias Pettersson scored on a first-period power play and Linus Karlsson and Filip Chytil made it 3-1 by the first intermission. Chytil's first two goals of the season came back to back, the second one shorthanded. Mark Stone's power-play goal early in the third pulled Vegas within 4-3 and tied the Golden Knights' franchise points record at 417, and 24 seconds later Drew O'Connor restored the two-goal lead. Karlsson's empty-netter capped his two-goal night, and Brock Boeser had two assists. Leevi Meriläinen stopped 34 of 37. Carter Hart stopped 21 of 26. Vancouver is still 4-17-1, but Vegas just lost at home to the team everyone else in the league is using as a tune-up, which should be a fun film session.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

NSH2SJS4Final: NSH 2, SJS 4

Nashville's seven-game win streak ended in San Jose, against a Sharks team that had played in Utah the night before. Will Smith and Collin Graf scored in the first, Ivar Stenberg made it 3-0 early in the second, and Macklin Celebrini put it away in the third, with Celebrini and Smith each finishing with a goal and two assists. Nils Hoglander and a late Steven Stamkos power-play goal were all the Predators had to show. Alex Nedeljkovic stopped 32 of 34; Juuse Saros stopped 20 of 24. The Sharks have won two in a row and three of their last four, with the kids doing the heavy lifting. Nashville flew all the way to California to remember what losing feels like, courtesy of a Sharks team that's still -18 on the season.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Sunday, November 15

Game recap

SEA1CAR5Final: SEA 1, CAR 5

Carolina packed up Helsinki with a 5-1 win and a two-game sweep of Seattle, which is a long way to fly to get your homework graded twice. The power play did the damage: Jackson Blake opened it up with the man advantage, and Andrei Svechnikov scored twice more on it, with Nikolaj Ehlers setting up three goals. Mark Jankowski chipped in two of his own, and Jordan Staal played 13:55 in his first game back after missing 14. Joey Daccord was pulled after letting in four on 14 shots, Philipp Grubauer stopped 22 of 23 the rest of the way, and Matty Beniers got Seattle's only goal. Pyotr Kochetkov needed just 12 saves, and Jagger Firkus made his NHL debut in a game that was over by the second intermission. The Kraken put 13 shots on net across a whole hockey game, about what they'd manage from the Climate Pledge parking lot.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

WPG5CHI4SOFinal: WPG 5, CHI 4 SO

Chicago led 4-0 midway through the second period and still lost, which takes a special kind of commitment. Tyler Bertuzzi, Anton Frondell and Connor Bedard (power play) chased Stuart Skinner after one period (three goals on eight shots), Frank Nazar made it 4-0 on another power play, and then the Blackhawks went back to being the Blackhawks. Mark Scheifele started the comeback at 16:05 of the second, Kyle Connor and Cole Perfetti (power play) followed, and Gabriel Vilardi tied it with 1:13 left and the goalie pulled. Scheifele finished with a goal and three assists, set the Jets' franchise points record, and scored in the shootout too; Connor added the winner there, with Patrick Kane the only Hawk to beat Nico Daws, who stopped 12 of 13 in relief. Spencer Knight made 27 saves. In Chicago a four-goal lead isn't a cushion, it's a loan, and the Jets called it in.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

MIN6BOS2Final: MIN 6, BOS 2

Minnesota walked into TD Garden and treated it like a rental: 6-2, an eighth straight road win and an 11-game point streak. Ryan Hartman scored twice, Danila Yurov scored twice (the second into an empty net), and Quinn Hughes and Blake Coleman also scored, Coleman adding two assists. Kirill Kaprizov set up two, and Brock Faber got an assist in his season debut, the kind of welcome-back gift most guys only get in their dreams. Fraser Minten on the power play and David Pastrnak cut it to 4-2, then Yurov answered 90 seconds later. Jesper Wallstedt stopped 30 of 32; Jeremy Swayman saw 24 shots and let five through. Marcus Foligno and Tanner Jeannot fought in the second, which was Boston's best stretch of the night. The Bruins wanted a statement game and got one: it just had the Wild's name on it.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

EDM1TOR0Final: EDM 1, TOR 0

Devon Levi got his first NHL shutout, and Toronto made it easy for him: 19 shots, all saved, in a 1-0 Oilers win. The only goal came at 15:34 of the second, Evan Bouchard finishing off Connor McDavid and Leon Draisaitl, which stretches McDavid's point streak to 21 games. Anthony Stolarz was terrific at the other end, 22 saves on 23, and got exactly the run support he's come to expect. John Tavares thought he'd tied it late, but the goal was waved off, the perfect ending to a homestand the Leafs finished 0-6, now six straight losses. Colton Dach and Brandon Duhaime fought in the first, the closest Toronto came to winning anything all night. Leafs fans paid full price to watch a team that can't score in its own building, which at least makes it a very Toronto tradition.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

COL4MTL1Final: COL 4, MTL 1

Colorado played its first game without Nathan MacKinnon and Cale Makar and won 4-1 in Montreal anyway, which is either great depth or a very bad sign for the Canadiens. It ended Montreal's 12-game point streak. Fedor Svechkov opened the scoring, Brock Nelson made it 2-0 with an extra attacker on late in the first, and after Nick Suzuki got one back in the second, Artturi Lehkonen scored his 15th on the power play and Nicolas Roy hit the empty net. Mackenzie Blackwood stopped 25 of 26, Jakub Dobes 23 of 26. Alex Gagne made his NHL debut beside Brent Burns, who played his 1,600th game, so the Avs' blue line went from first night to forever on one pair. Montreal spent two weeks looking like a contender and then lost to the Avalanche's understudies.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

DET2TBL0Final: DET 2, TBL 0

Daniil Tarasov stopped all 31 shots and Detroit won 2-0 in Tampa, ending its five-game skid and the Lightning's home streak in one go. Lucas Raymond scored the only goal that mattered, at 13:12 of the second from William Wallinder, and set up Michael Brandsegg-Nygård's empty-netter with 43 seconds left. Andrei Vasilevskiy was nearly as good, 20 saves on 21, and lost anyway, because Tampa played without Anthony Cirelli and Erik Cernak and couldn't solve a goalie who got the start after John Gibson gave up five in Florida. The Red Wings needed a win like they need Dylan Larkin to pick up the phone, and they got one. Tampa had 31 shots and zero goals, the hockey version of working a double and going home broke.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

OTT4PIT1Final: OTT 4, PIT 1

Linus Ullmark picked up his 200th NHL win in Pittsburgh, and the Penguins barely made him work for it: 16 saves on 17 in a 4-1 Senators win that runs Ottawa's point streak to five. Tommy Novak gave Pittsburgh a lead with eight seconds left in the first, and that was the last fun the home crowd had. Michael Amadio tied it with an unassisted goal and then set up Claude Giroux, Tim Stützle added his 11th in the third, and Thomas Chabot finished it into the empty net. Sergei Murashov kept it close with 30 saves on 33. Ottawa outshot Pittsburgh 34-17, which is the kind of gap you usually see between the NHL and the AHL. The Penguins are 7-11-2 and Kyle Dubas is reportedly warming up the sell button, and nights like this are why.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

NJD7WSH4Final: NJD 7, WSH 4

Washington threw 47 shots at Connor Hellebuyck, scored four, and still lost 7-4, because the Devils got their own goalie and the Capitals got whatever Charlie Lindgren was doing (26 saves on 32). Hellebuyck made 43 saves and is 7-0-0 as a Devil, a franchise record. The Caps led three times in the first, 1-0, 2-1 and 3-2, on goals from Pierre-Luc Dubois, Ryan Leonard and Anthony Beauvillier, and Cole Hutson set up three. Then New Jersey took over: Jesper Boqvist tied it, Timo Meier scored on the power play, and Nico Hischier's shorthanded goal 56 seconds into the third was the winner. Evan Rodrigues scored twice, Lenni Hameenaho had a goal and two assists, and Luke Hughes three assists, while Anton Silaev made his NHL debut. The Capitals outshot the Devils by 15 and lost by three, which is advanced stats' way of saying 'nice try.'

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

PHI4CBJ3Final: PHI 4, CBJ 3

Columbus scored twice in the first 4:19 on home ice, and the Flyers, a team that scores like it's paying per goal, answered with four. Dmitri Voronkov's first of the season and Matthew Knies put the Blue Jackets up 2-0. Trevor Zegras, an unassisted Matvei Michkov and a Denver Barkey power-play goal made it 3-2 early in the second; Adam Fantilli tied it, and Barkey won it at 11:54 of the third off Noel Acciari's setup. Joseph Woll stopped 28 of 31, Jet Greaves 17 of 21, and Owen Tippett and Dante Fabbro fought in the second. Columbus played without Sean Monahan and is 7-11-0. Blowing a two-goal lead to the Flyers' offense is like getting outrun by a Zamboni.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

FLA4STL1Final: FLA 4, STL 1

St. Louis honored Keith Tkachuk before the game, and his sons said thanks by beating the Blues: Brady Tkachuk scored the power-play opener, with Matthew Tkachuk on the assist, in a 4-1 Florida win. Dmitry Kulikov scored his first of the season a minute later, Anton Lundell made it 3-0 in the second, and Sam Reinhart's unassisted goal in the third, his 12th, came on a night he reached 700 career points. Jacob Markstrom stopped 23 of 24 and lost the shutout to Dylan Holloway's power-play goal with 2:06 left. Joel Hofer made 24 saves on 28 in his fourth straight start. Radko Gudas played his 900th game. It was a lovely ceremony for the Tkachuk family, and then the family took two points home to Florida, the most Blues thing imaginable.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

BUF0DAL2Final: BUF 0, DAL 2

Jamie Benn got his 1,000th career point, every one of them in a Dallas sweater, and it was the goal that beat Buffalo 2-0. Benn scored at 16:23 of the second off Justin Hryckowian and Nils Lundkvist, and Wyatt Johnston added a power-play goal with 42 seconds left. Jake Oettinger needed only 22 saves for his fourth shutout, which says a lot about the Sabres' night. Alex Lyon was good in his second straight start, 28 saves on 30, and got nothing for it. Dallas is 11-6-2; Buffalo is 8-8-4 and has now been shut out by a goalie who could have played the third period in a recliner. A thousand points for Benn, zero for the Sabres: that's been the Buffalo experience for about 15 years.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

SJS6UTA5SOFinal: SJS 6, UTA 5 SO

Ten goals in 65 minutes, two fights and a shootout, and San Jose came out of Utah with a 6-5 win and Utah with a fifth straight loss. Zac Jones scored twice as Utah led 3-1 and 4-3, but the Sharks kept coming: Tyler Toffoli and Adam Gaudette on the power play, Zack Ostapchuk, then Eric Pohlkamp's first NHL goal to tie it at 4 in the third. Dmitry Orlov put the Sharks ahead with 5:43 left and finished with four points; Barrett Hayton tied it again on the power play two minutes later. In the shootout Vincent Trocheck and Macklin Celebrini traded goals before Mason Marchment won it in the fifth round. Karel Vejmelka gave up five on 21 shots (Andre Tourigny said afterward 'Vej has to be better'), and Yaroslav Askarov made 27 saves. Andrew Peeke fought Ty Dellandrea and then Gaudette. Utah's defense went the full 65 minutes without showing up, a real commitment to the bit.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

NYI6ANA2Final: NYI 6, ANA 2

Simon Holmstrom picked a good night for his first career hat trick: the Islanders beat Anaheim 6-2, and Mathew Barzal got an assist on Ben Hutton's goal 1:55 into his season debut. Bo Horvat scored on the power play, Holmstrom scored twice in 5:27 of the second, Mitchell Chaffee made it 5-1, and Holmstrom finished the job early in the third. Matthew Schaefer had three assists, because apparently the 19-year-old is also the Isles' playmaker now. Semyon Varlamov stopped 26 of 28; Lukas Dostal stayed in for all 60 minutes and six goals on 25 shots, which is the kind of loyalty usually reserved for a bad contract. Nikita Nesterenko and Cutter Gauthier (his 17th) scored for the Ducks. The Ducks were down 5-1 before the game was half over, then left their goalie out there to absorb a sixth: that's not goaltending support, that's a dare.

Game recap

CGY3LAK2Final: CGY 3, LAK 2

Calgary opened its road trip with a 3-2 win in Los Angeles, and the Kings helped. Morgan Frost scored early in the second off a Cody Ceci turnover, and Ceci watched the third period from the bench. Joel Armia tied it at 6:21 of the third, Matvei Gridin answered five minutes later for the winner, and Yegor Sharangovich hit the empty net with 1:14 left. Mats Zuccarello's first of the season with the goalie pulled made it close 18 seconds later. Dustin Wolf stopped 29 of 31; Anton Forsberg 21 of 23. The Kings are 5-11-2, level with Chicago at 12 points and ahead of only Vancouver, a Hollywood ending nobody in LA wanted to see.

Saturday, November 14

Game recap

NYR5VAN1Final: NYR 5, VAN 1

Vancouver hung around for a period, which at this point counts as a moral victory. Elias Pettersson opened the scoring at 12:13 of the first, Gabe Perreault answered before intermission, and then the second period happened: four Rangers goals in 7:49. Oliver Bjorkstrand scored on the power play, Glenn Gawdin got his first NHL goal unassisted, Alexis Lafrenière buried his 10th, and Gawdin added his second just 56 seconds later. A guy who played 7:59 had two goals; the entire Canucks lineup had one. J.T. Miller set up two against his old team, Dylan Garand stopped 27 of 28, and Leevi Meriläinen made 26 saves on 31. New York is 12-8-1. Vancouver is 3-17-1 with seven straight losses, and the only thing the Canucks are building right now is a lottery ticket.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

NSH3VGK2SOFinal: NSH 3, VGK 2 SO

Vegas threw 42 shots at Juuse Saros and got two past him, so naturally this one needed a shootout. Ryan O'Reilly scored at 7:56 of the first, Victor Olofsson tied it, and Rasmus Andersson put Vegas ahead in the second. O'Reilly tied it again at 9:44 of the third, his second of the night and ninth of the season, and overtime settled nothing. In the shootout Trevor Connelly scored for Vegas, Filip Forsberg answered, Jack Eichel was stopped and Roman Josi ended it, after playing 31:40 and apparently still having legs. Saros made 40 saves; Adin Hill made 30 on 32. Nashville has won seven straight and is 11-4-5. Vegas outshot its guests by 10 and went home with one point, which in that town is called breaking even and still feels like losing.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →
